AI can already cut, caption and format a clip for you. Free GitHub skills teach Claude the editing part in minutes. So why isn't everyone going viral off podcast clips? Because editing was never the hard part. Choosing the moment is. AI does not know which 47 seconds out of a two hour conversation deserve to become the clip. No context. No content intelligence. Here is how you build that layer. Scrape the latest 100 clips from the biggest podcast short form accounts. Steven Bartlett, Chris Williamson, Alex Hormozi, anyone running serious long form volume. Capture views, post date, duration, transcript, text overlay and format. Then scrape their original long form episodes and pull the complete transcripts with timestamps. The timestamps are non negotiable. They are what lets Claude match every clip back to the exact episode and the exact moment it came from. Now you reverse engineer the decision. Why those 47 seconds. Where the clip starts. What context got removed. Whether the payoff moved forward. What spoken hook, text overlay and format they used. And how it performed against that account's normal clips. Run enough of these and the patterns surface. Turn the patterns into a Claude skill that understands how the best podcast teams select and package their clips. Then hand it any new timestamped transcript. It returns the strongest moments, exact timestamps, hook options, text overlays, formats and editing instructions. The editing skill does the easy part. None of this needs new software. The tools exist. The clipping skills exist. The data is public. Nobody is assembling it into an intelligence layer. Impossible to fail does not mean every clip goes viral. It means every clip starts with real evidence, and every result makes the next selection smarter. Build the selection layer first. The edit is the easy bit.

Hit follow and share your most UNHINGED tip! Automation comes last, not first. Asking AI for an answer is stage 1. The work gets more useful when you use AI to test ideas, learn your process, and handle bigger jobs with clear rules. The 5 stages: 1. Ask AI: Get an answer. 2. Think with AI: Find gaps in your ideas. 3. Teach AI: Show it how you like work done. 4. Delegate to AI: Give it a meaningful assignment. 5. Automate with AI: Have it repeat the work on a schedule. At stage 2, ask AI to find blind spots and question whether the work needs to exist. At stage 3, give AI context, examples, rules, and feedback. Let it ask questions. Check the output, then save your process as a reusable skill. At stage 4, give AI a real job with several files. Check every figure and piece of evidence before you trust the result. At stage 5, schedule a reliable skill. Start with drafts for human review. Add tools or connectors when the job needs fresh data. Get the full 5-stage guide here: https://www.sabrina.dev/p/5-stages-of-ai-mastery What are the 5 stages of AI mastery? How do I teach AI how I work? Hit follow and share your most UNHINGED tip! AI isn't reading your mind. Most weak ChatGPT answers start with a weak request. These 6 prompt add-ons help AI ask better questions, copy your taste, spot weak thinking, and check its work. 1. ELI10 Add this when an answer feels too hard. ChatGPT will explain the idea in simple terms. 2. Before you answer, ask me 5 clarifying questions. Use this when your request needs more detail. Your answers give ChatGPT the context it needs. 3. Here's examples I like: [examples] Paste samples you like and dislike. AI gets a clear target instead of guessing. 4. Turn this chat into a reusable skill. This turns your working chat into instructions for later. You won't need to repeat the full setup. 5. Find my blind spots and weak assumptions Ask this before you trust the answer. It pushes AI to challenge your logic instead of praising every idea. 6. Keep improving this until it meets these RULES. Check your work against each rule before saying you're done. Give AI your rules first. Then it checks each one and keeps fixing the output before it stops. How do I write better ChatGPT prompts? What prompts improve AI answers?
